title: What are the smallest and largest gaps between primes up to 100?
description: The primes up to a hundred are written in order and the gap between each neighbouring pair is read off. The smallest gap and the largest gap are then checked against the numbers lying between the primes.
teaching_notes: One idea: the gap between successive primes is found by subtracting neighbours in the list, and a long gap is one with only composite numbers inside. Watch for students who count the numbers between two primes instead of subtracting them.

video_script.why: The child reads the gaps from the list of primes that the circling and crossing out gave, and finds the smallest and the largest.
video_script.substitution: Take away each prime from the next one in the list and compare the gaps.
video_script.anchor: The list of primes up to 100 written in a row, with a gap marked between neighbours
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest gap is one, from two to three. The largest gap is eight, from eighty nine to ninety seven.

final_answer.spoken: the gaps run from one to eight

maths_rules: 3 - 2 = 1; after 2 every prime is odd, so each later gap is at least 2
no other gap in the list is bigger than 8
video_script.design: The row of primes is drawn with each gap written above it; the smallest gap is circled in teal and the largest in amber.

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, start at the front. Three take away two is one.
<bookmark mark='odd'/>After two, every prime is odd, so each later gap is at least two. That makes one the smallest gap.

narration: <bookmark mark='six'/>Step two, look for the long gaps. From twenty three to twenty nine is a gap of six, and several others are six too.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>The longest one comes later. Ninety seven take away eighty nine is eight.

narration: <bookmark mark='between'/>Step three, check the long gap. The numbers from ninety to ninety six lie between the two primes.
<bookmark mark='none'/>Each of them is composite. Ninety one is seven times thirteen, and the others are even or multiples of three or five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The smallest gap is one, from two to three. The largest gap is eight, from eighty nine to ninety seven.
